rachmaninoff-prelude-23-1.title: Prelude in F-sharp minor, Op. 23 No. 1
rachmaninoff-prelude-23-1.subtitle: Sergei Rachmaninoff · solo piano · complete · advanced

guide.text: The initial pickup belongs to the low ornamental approach. Listen to the flowing left hand before the right-hand F-sharp–E melody enters.
Compare this answering statement with the opening. The melody holds long notes while the chromatic accompaniment keeps moving.
Follow the rising register and then the octave melody. Isolate the moving inner voices to hear how the texture grows.
The bass descends and the free left-hand run climbs out of the low register. Practice bars 24–28 divide that unmeasured run; their numbers differ from the printed edition.
The octave melody continues above dense moving chords and further free runs. Practice bars 31–33 and 36–38 divide those runs for navigation.
Hear the texture settle and recognize the opening melody again. Compare the return with the first statement.
The moving material changes hands and rises through the registers before descending. Keep the melody distinct from the inner notes.
Listen for the repeated F-sharp-minor sonorities and the sustained final chord. The player uses a steady practice tempo rather than the edition’s tempo changes.

source.label: Abel Cheung · Mutopia 1958 · after Muzyka and Gutheil editions. Adapted to interactive notation under CC BY-SA 4.0. Practice bar numbers split the source’s unmeasured runs into short navigation units; compare the printed edition. Free runs use their written durations at the fixed practice tempo. Pedal, slur shaping and expressive timing are not reproduced.

rachmaninoff-prelude-23-4.title: Prelude in D major, Op. 23 No. 4
rachmaninoff-prelude-23-4.subtitle: Sergei Rachmaninoff · solo piano · complete · advanced

guide.text: Hear the left-hand introduction and the sustained upper melody. Keep the triplet accompaniment even as the melody crosses the pulse.
Follow the changing upper notes over the wide left-hand pattern. Isolate a hand, then listen to the voices together.
Compare the returning phrase shapes and their altered harmony. Loop a few bars to hear where the inner voices move.
Trace the descending phrases and the tied D in bar 31. Cross-staff triplet gaps remain exact; the printed source helps explain the overlapping voices.
The texture becomes more chordal while the bass keeps moving. Follow the upper line through each short phrase.
Listen as the phrases climb and the chords spread into the high register. Compare the upper melody with the changing bass.
Recognize the opening phrase at a higher register with fuller chords. Keep the melodic octave line above the accompaniment.
The high-register statement continues toward a quieter ending. Compare its changing chord colors with the opening.
Follow the settling voices and final D-major sonority. Let the held notes connect across barlines; the practice tempo remains steady.

rachmaninoff-prelude-23-6.title: Prelude in E-flat major, Op. 23 No. 6
rachmaninoff-prelude-23-6.subtitle: Sergei Rachmaninoff · solo piano · complete · advanced

guide.text: Hear the octave melody above the continuous left-hand sixteenths. Compare the long upper notes with the moving bass.
The opening returns with extra chromatic motion and fuller chords. Follow the tied C in bar 8 while other chord tones change.
The melody moves into a higher register. Listen for the longer notes within the changing octave and chord shapes.
Follow the expanding register and denser harmony toward the high C. Use a slow loop to separate the melody from the accompaniment.
The texture thins and the opening material returns in a lower register. Listen for the chromatic inner lines and the bass changes.
Short fragments answer one another across the keyboard. Trace the upper notes while listening to the continuous left-hand motion.
The voices continue to exchange fragments. Isolate each hand to find where the melodic line sits before recombining them.
The upper line descends across the keyboard and settles into the final E-flat-major chord. Compare the quiet closing register with the earlier climax.
